 Coram:Honourable Mr. Justice Hasmukh D. Suthar
ORAL ORDER 1. RULE.
Learned APP waives service of rule for the respondent-State.

2. The present application is filed under Section 483 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (for short "BNSS") for regular bail in connection with FIR being C.R. No.11200038242202 of 2024 registered with Pardi Police Station, Valsad for the offences punishable under Sections 363, 376(1)
and 114 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (for short "IPC") / The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (for short "BNS") and Sections 4, 6 and 17 of the POCSO Act.
3. Learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the applicant submits that the applicant has nothing to do with the offence and he is falsely implicated in the offence.

It is submitted that in NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/20154/2024 ORDER DATED: 12/12/2024 undefined the FIR the complainant alleged that the complainant met a girl named Vishakha near Udvada Station Road,
Vijaybhai @ Kalu S/O Vishvanath ... vs State Of Gujarat on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/18181752/
1 and they became friends, exchanging phone numbers and speaking regularly.

On 18/06/2024,
Vishakha invited the complainant to accompany her to a bank in Udvada.
They traveled together to Valsad and then Vapi, visiting Namdha Lake.

When no trains were available for their return,
Vishakha called her friends, and three men arrived in a Swift car at Vapi Gunjan Rasta: Alibhai (driver), Dhruvil (front passenger), and Vijay (Vishakha's boyfriend).

The complainant, Vishakha,
and Vijay left the car near Viram Hotel, Pardi, and proceeded on Vijay's scooter to a secluded hut near Gangaji Khadi, where they were later joined by Dhruvil and another man, Raj.
Vishakha told the complainant that Dhruvil liked her and encouraged her to talk to him.
Later, Vishakha and Vijay left, leaving the complainant alone with Dhruvil.
Dhruvil then forcibly kissed her, removed her clothes, and sexually assaulted her.
The group stayed overnight at the hut, and the next day, the complainant was dropped home by the co-accused.

However, the present applicant has been implicated in the offence solely on the basis of suspicion that he transported the victim and the co-accused on his Activa scooter, even though he was not present at the scene.

It is further submitted that Accused No. 3, Dhruvil, is the main accused who committed the offence, whereas the applicant had no involvement in the crime, neither establishing any physical relations with anyone nor kidnapping anyone.
It is further submitted that, considering the nature of the offence, the applicant may be granted regular bail with the imposition of suitable conditions.
NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/20154/2024 ORDER DATED: 12/12/2024 undefined 4.
The learned APP and the learned advocate for the complainant have jointly opposed the grant of regular bail, citing the nature and gravity of the offence.
It is submitted that the applicant is directly involved in the offence of kidnapping and has past criminal antecedent.
The applicant is the person who abetted the offence, and an abettor is equally liable for the commission of the offence.
The applicant was fully aware of the incident that was going to happen to the victim.
Therefore, the present application may be dismissed.

5. While granting bail, the Court has to consider the involvement of the accused in the alleged offence, the jurisdiction to grant bail has to be exercised on the basis of the well settled principles having regard to the facts and circumstances of each case and the following factors are to be taken into consideration while considering an application for bail: (i) the nature of accusation and the severity of the punishment and the nature of the materials relied upon by the prosecution; (ii)
reasonable apprehension of tampering with the witnesses and threat to the complainant or the witnesses; (iii) reasonable possibility of securing the presence of the accused at the time of trial or the likelihood of his abscondence; (iv) character behaviour and standing of the accused and the circumstances which are peculiar to the accused; (v) larger interest of thThe allegation against the present applicant is that he only abetted the offence, and he played no role in the kidnapping or any other offence, including those under the POCSO Act.e public or the State and similar other considerations are required to be considered.
NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/20154/2024 ORDER DATED: 12/12/2024 undefined 6.
I have heard the learned advocates appearing on behalf of the respective parties and perused the investigation papers.

Following aspects have been considered:

sentences.text:
(1) The applicant is in jail since 20.06.2024; (2) Investigation is over and charge-sheet is filed; (3) The allegation against the present applicant is that the complainant befriended Vishakha near Udvada Station Road, and on 18.06.2024,
they traveled together to Valsad and Vapi, visiting Namdha Lake.

After finding no train to return, Vishakha called her friends, and they were picked up by three men namely, Alibhai (driver), Dhruvil (front passenger), and Vijay (Vishakha's boyfriend)
in a Swift car.
They traveled to a secluded hut near Gangaji Khadi, where Vishakha introduced Dhruvil to the complainant.
Later, Vishakha and Vijay left, leaving the complainant alone with Dhruvil, who sexually assaulted her.
The next day, the complainant was dropped home by the co- accused.

(4) Prima faice, it appears that the applicant only abetted the offence and played no role in the kidnapping or any other offence, including those under the POCSO Act, nor did he sexually assault anyone.

(5) Now, nothing is required to be discovered or recovered from the accused and there is no possibility of the trial taking place in the near future;
7.

This Court has also taken into consideration the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Sanjay Chandra NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/20154/2024 ORDER DATED: 12/12/2024 undefined vs. Central Bureau of Investigation reported in [2012]1 SCC 40 as well as in the case of Gudikanti Narasimhulu And Ors vs. Public Prosecutor, High Court of Andhra Pradesh reported in (1978)1 SCC 240.

sentences.text: Obviously, the conclusion of trial will take time and keeping the accused behind the bars is nothing but amounts to pre-trial conviction and therefore, considering the celebrated principle of bail jurisprudence is that "bail is a rule and jail is exception" as well as the concept of personal liberty guaranteed under Article 21 of the Constitution of India, present application deserves consideration .

8. In the facts and circumstances of the case and considering the nature of the allegations made against the applicant/s in the FIR, without discussing the evidence in detail, prima facie, this Court is of the opinion that this is a fit case to exercise the discretion and enlarge the applicant/s on regular bail.
Hence, the present application is allowed.

sentences.text: If the applicant is found in any illegal activity or any similar type of activity, then, concerned Investigating Officer shall have liberty to file an application for cancellation of bail against the present applicant.
The authorities will release the applicant/s only if he is not required in connection with any other offence for the time being.

If breach of any of the above conditions is committed, the Sessions Judge concerned will be free to issue warrant or take NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/20154/2024 ORDER DATED: 12/12/2024 undefined appropriate action in the matter.
10. Bail bond to be executed before the lower Court having jurisdiction to try the case.
It will be open for the concerned Court to delete, modify and/or relax any of the above conditions, in accordance with law.
11 At the trial, the trial Court shall not be influenced by the observations of preliminary nature qua the evidence at this stage made by this Court while enlarging the applicant/ on bail.
12. Rule is made absolute to the aforesaid extent.
Direct service is permitted.
